text:
Cutter Gauthier has 17 goals in his last ten games. Read that again. Twenty points in that stretch, and our numbers say it's earned: he's getting more chances on his own stick (5.8 expected goals against 4.9 usual) and nearly two more minutes a night. It has turned an old trade back into a headline, with Flyers general manager Daniel Briere publicly pushing back on an Elliotte Friedman report about the deal that sent Gauthier to Anaheim. Mikael Granlund, the Ducks' captain, is on pace for 100 points by The Hockey News' count, and Beckett Sennecke has 16 points in ten.

The trouble in Anaheim is everything behind the scoring. The Ducks have lost four of five, were shut out in Colorado on Thursday, and take only 46% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances). Lukas Dostal is .857 on the season and 5.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and the team sent Laurent Brossoit back to the AHL despite a 4-1 record. Ryan Poehling is out with a knee.

Utah might be the unluckiest good team in the league. The Mammoth take 57% of the expected goals at five on five, best in this matchup by a distance, yet their goal difference is even on plus 14.9 expected. Finishing (5.4 goals short) and goaltending (Karel Vejmelka at 6.3 below expected) have eaten the difference. Injuries hurt too: Dylan Guenther and Nick Schmaltz are on injured reserve, so Vincent Trocheck is playing 23 minutes a night on the top line and Kailer Yamamoto has moved onto the first power play. Logan Cooley has 14 points in his last ten, though a punch on Vancouver's Linus Karlsson drew a look from the league.

Wednesday's win over Colorado snapped a six-game winless run and, by the sound of it, started a rivalry. Our playoff race has Utah at 70% and Anaheim at 47%. Utah takes 4.8 penalties a game, which is the opening for a Ducks power play with a shooter this hot.
headline: Gauthier's tear meets a Mammoth team owed some luck
